title: a clippy diagnostic on a Rust file the branch touches

explain.what: The head's clippy log names a Rust file the branch touches (LR/clippy::<lint>, or LR/<rustc lint>).
explain.why: CI runs clippy with -D warnings, so main is clean and a diagnostic on a touched file is new. Choppa never builds: he reads the log the head's own gate wrote.
explain.fix: Fix what the diagnostic says and run clippy again. A diagnostic that must stay needs a waiver for LR/<lint>.

no-evidence.what: No clippy log for this head: the branch touches Rust files and nothing shows clippy ran on them.
no-evidence.why: Choppa reads clippy, never runs it (a build takes minutes). CI still gates it; this only says the run end could not see it.
no-evidence.fix: Run the crate's clippy at the head and keep its output: `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings 2>&1 | tee "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/norn/clippy/$(git rev-parse HEAD).log"`.

config-changed.what: The branch edits clippy's config (clippy.toml, or a [lints] table of a Cargo.toml).
config-changed.why: The config says what clippy looks for; editing it is the cheapest way to clear a finding.
config-changed.fix: Keep the config as it is, or ask the owner: his waiver for LR/config-changed approves the rule change.
